## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | Coral holobiont DNA diluted to **4 ng µL⁻¹** |
| **Output** | ITS2 amplicons with Illumina overhangs, checked on a gel, ready for indexing/sequencing |
| **Reaction** | 25 µL, Phusion master mix, in duplicate |
| **Time** | ~2 h PCR + 1 h gel (estimate) |
| **Tested on** | *Porites astreoides* (healthy, partially dead and bleached); *Montipora capitata* |

This page covers the **PCR and gel check**. Primer sequences, pooling and sequencing submission follow the Putnam Lab [ITS2 sequencing protocol](https://github.com/emmastrand/EmmaStrand_Notebook/blob/master/_posts/2020-01-31-ITS2-Sequencing-Protocol.md).

::: {.callout-warning}
## Low-symbiont samples
When symbiont density is very low (e.g. bleached corals), the standard PCR can amplify **coral** DNA instead of ITS2: faint bands, or bands of the wrong size. The cycling options below raise annealing stringency to fix this.
:::

## Materials

- Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (2×)
- ITS2 forward and reverse primers with Illumina adapter overhangs, 10 µM
- Ultrapure water; DNA at 4 ng µL⁻¹
- Positive control (DNA that amplified before) and a no-template negative control
- Thermocycler; agarose gel equipment (1% gel)

## Procedure

### A. Master mix

1. Number of reactions = (samples + 1 positive + 1 negative + 1 spare) × **2** (duplicate wells).
2. Per well:

   | Reagent | µL |
   |---|---|
   | Phusion Master Mix (2×) | 12.5 |
   | F primer (10 µM) | 0.5 |
   | R primer (10 µM) | 0.5 |
   | Ultrapure water | 10.5 |
   | **Master mix total** | **24** |
   | DNA (4 ng µL⁻¹) | 1 |

   e.g. 4 samples + controls + spare = 7 × 2 = 14 wells → 175 µL Phusion, 7 µL each primer, 147 µL water.
3. Add **24 µL** master mix per well, then **1 µL** DNA (water for the negative). Seal, mix, and spin down.

### B. Cycling: choose one

| Program | Use when | Cycling |
|---|---|---|
| **High-annealing** | Primers with Illumina adapter tails (used Apr 2022) | 95 °C 3 min → **35 ×** (95 °C 30 s, **71 °C** 30 s, 72 °C 30 s) → 72 °C 2 min → 4 °C |
| **TD-1** (Korbie & Mattick 2008, Tm 52 °C) | Low-symbiont samples | 95 °C 3 min → **11 cycles** of 95 °C 30 s / anneal 45 s stepping **62 → 52 °C** (−1 °C per cycle) / 72 °C 60 s → **25 ×** at 52 °C → 72 °C 5 min |
| **TD-2** | Low-symbiont samples | As TD-1, but step down **62 → 47 °C** (Tm − 5) over 16 cycles, then **20 ×** at 47 °C |
| **TD-3** (modified from H. Putnam) | Low-symbiont samples | 95 °C 7 min → **20 ×** (94 °C 30 s, 62 °C 30 s, −0.5 °C per cycle, 72 °C 1 min) → **12 ×** at 52 °C → 72 °C 7 min |

The 71 °C annealing is the calculated Tm of the primers *including* the Illumina adapter tails, which is why it is more specific than the original program.

::: {.callout-important}
## Which program to use
In March 2022, TD-1 did **not** give clean bands; TD-2 and TD-3 were compared on a gel ([2022-03-16](../notebook/2022-03-16-touchdown-pcr-for-its2.md)). In April 2022, the high-annealing (71 °C) program was used for the Porites July Bleaching re-sequencing ([2022-03-19](../notebook/2022-03-21-20220319-pjb-its2-re-seq.md)). TODO: record which program gave the best bands and make it the default here.
:::

### C. Gel check

4. Run an aliquot of each reaction (e.g. 5 µL) on a **1% agarose gel** (75–100 V) with a ladder.
5. Expect one clean band at the ITS2 amplicon size (TODO: add expected size with adapters) in samples and the positive control, and **nothing** in the negative.
6. Pool duplicate wells and continue with cleanup/indexing per the Putnam Lab protocol.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Faint or no band in bleached samples | Very few symbiont templates; coral DNA out-competes | Use a touchdown or 71 °C program; check DNA concentration |
| Band at the wrong size | Off-target (coral) amplification | Raise annealing stringency (71 °C or touchdown) |
| One sample much brighter than the rest | Uneven template | Re-check the 4 ng µL⁻¹ dilution |
| Band in the negative control | Contamination | New water and primer aliquots; clean the PCR area |
